{"name": "charge-review", "steps": "Inputs: the developer's org or account id, the invoice (id or month), the lines and amounts they mean, request ids if they have them.

1. Identify the account. If you have neither org nor account id, ask_developer for org_id (plus invoice_id/invoice_month and line_items/amounts/request_ids in the same call if not given). lookup_account.
2. Check billing channel, plan and has_signed_contract on the account.
   - Not billed directly by Redwood: search_knowledge for the procedure for that exact channel (cloud marketplace vs reseller are different pages; apply only the one matching billing_channel). Support credits/disputes nothing there; tell the developer who bills them and where refunds/credits/invoices go. Open a case only if the current page says so (e.g. a metering mismatch).
3. get_invoice (map a month to an id from lookup_account's invoice list). Read console_confirmed_duplicates (original_line vs copy_lines, decided by where the usage records point), same_requests_but_unconfirmed, and same_amount_but_different_requests. get_usage for request ids the developer gave.
4. Classify:
   a. Console-confirmed duplicate: act only on the copy line, never the original.
   b. Look-alike (same amount/description, different request ids), no second line, or usage pointing to neither/both lines: NOT a confirmed duplicate. Say so plainly with the console evidence. Never say a credit is likely before the console confirms a duplicate.
   c. Wrong rate/quantity/product, unrecognized usage, retries/cancelled streams, token mismatch: search the usage/token pages; if they explain it, explain and stop.
   d. Waive/reduce a correct charge (goodwill, exception, SLA credit, refund): not Support's to issue. Load team-handoff.
5. For (a), search_knowledge for what Support may do now: the Support charter (which accounts Support may credit at all), the credits-and-disputes page, and Finance's approval matrix for the per-line limit. The limit can depend on how the invoice was rated (e.g. which price book applies to the invoice's usage period): search the Finance close calendar for that, using the invoice period. Drafts, proposals and threads change nothing.
   - Support may credit this account and the copy line's full amount is within the limit: confirm_with_developer "I'll issue a credit note of $X (full amount) on the duplicated line L of invoice I." Only after yes: issue_credit_note (reason duplicate, memo with request ids). Tell them the credit note id and amount, and when it applies if the page says. No handoff.
   - Over the limit, or an account Support may not credit (e.g. contract/enterprise per the charter): do not credit or split. confirm_with_developer "I'll open a dispute on line L of invoice I (duplicate charge, request ids R) and hand it to Billing Ops." After yes: open_dispute, then load team-handoff and escalate with the dispute id.
   - If the developer says no: write nothing (no credit, dispute or case); say nothing was changed and they can come back.
6. For (b) and unexplained (c): gather intake (invoice, both lines, window in the account's billing timezone, request ids, what they checked) with ask_developer, then load team-handoff.
7. Never promise a dispute outcome or date. If a write is rejected, read get_invoice to see the state before saying anything."}

body: ## Purpose
The support console can look up a customer's billing account, issue a credit note against invoice lines, and open a billing dispute. This page defines when Support uses each one. It amends the billing routing page for duplicate charges only; everything else on that page still applies. This version is effective from 26 February 2027 and adds how to tell the copy from the original. Support's per-line limit is set in Finance's Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix (Finance shared drive), which FP&A revised in February 2027; check the matrix for the limit that applies to the invoice in front of you."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-console-duplicate-charges-and-disputes-2027.json", "chunk": "7/7", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes (v2)", "status": "published", "date": "2027-02-26", "text": "## Common mistakes
- Crediting the original line instead of the copy.
- Crediting a line because two lines share a description or an amount, without matching request IDs.
- Splitting a line over the limit into several credits.
- Crediting a marketplace purchase: the marketplace bills those, so Support has nothing to credit.
- Telling the customer a dispute will succeed, or when Billing Ops will finish.
## Questions
Ask in #support-billing. Page owner: Dev Patel.

- Look up the customer's billing account in the console before you quote an amount, a plan, an invoice line, or whether a charge is a duplicate. You can find the account by its account id or by the customer's org name; ask for one of them if the customer hasn't given either.
- Quote amounts as the console shows them. Don't restate a figure the customer gives you as fact.
## Duplicate charges: what Support may credit
A charge is a confirmed duplicate only when the console shows two lines on the same direct Redwood invoice that bill the same request IDs. A similar description or the same amount on its own is not enough.

|---|---|

body: ## Purpose
This charter is the source of truth for what the support agent may and may not do. It takes precedence over proposals, drafts, Slack threads, and older pages where they disagree.
## Credits and disputes
- Support can issue duplicate-charge credit notes only on self-serve accounts.
- Support may not issue a credit note of any amount on an account with a signed contract (Enterprise).
- For a confirmed duplicate on a contract account, open a dispute on the duplicated line (reason `duplicate_charge`, with the request IDs) and hand the case to Billing Ops with the invoice number, the line and the dispute id. Billing Ops applies contract-account adjustments under the contract."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-console-billing-credits-and-disputes.json", "chunk": "4/4", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes", "status": "published SUPERSEDED by 'Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes (v2)' effective 2027-02-26", "date": "2026-02-05", "text": "## What Support never credits
- Goodwill, exceptions, SLA credits, or any credit someone says a manager, sales rep or Redwood engineer already approved. These stay with Finance, per the #support guidance from FP&A. Route the request; don't issue anything from the console.
- Marketplace purchases, which are billed by the marketplace.
## Telling the customer
- Say what you did: the credit note and its amount, or that a dispute is open and Billing Ops has the case. Don't promise the outcome of a dispute or a date.

{"query": "Finance 2027 Close Calendar Invoice Periods price book applicable usage August 2026 invoices", "results": [{"source": "sources/google_drive/shared_drives/finance/2027-close-calendar-and-invoice-periods.json", "chunk": "3/4", "kind": "Drive doc", "title": "2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods", "status": "final", "date": "2027-02-22", "text": "## Late usage
Usage that reaches the warehouse after BD1 is not added to an issued invoice. It is billed on the next month's invoice as a separate line marked "prior-period usage" with the original dates, so a customer comparing a month's export to its invoice may see those requests a month later.
## Price changes
A price-book change applies to usage from the first period that starts on or after its effective date. Mid-period changes are not prorated unless the order form says so.

content: ## Purpose
This page sets the 2027 monthly close for usage-based invoices: when each month's invoices are cut, which usage lands in which invoice period, and how late usage is handled. Billing Ops, Telemetry and Support use it when a customer asks what a month's invoice covers.
## Monthly close calendar
| Business day | Step | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| BD1 | Usage for the closed month is frozen in the metering warehouse | Telemetry |
| BD2 | Usage is rated against the account's price book and invoice lines are drafted | Billing Ops |
| BD3 | Variance review: lines more than 25% above the prior month are checked against usage | Billing Ops |
| BD4 | Invoices are issued and autopay is attempted on the due date shown on the invoice | Billing Ops |
| BD5 | Revenue for the month is booked and the period is closed | Accounting |"}, {"source": "sources/google_drive/shared_drives/finance/2027-price-book-rollout-plan.json", "chunk": "1/1", "kind": "Drive doc", "title": "2027 price book rollout plan (DRAFT)", "status": "draft", "date": "2026-12-15", "text": "title: 2027 price book rollout plan (DRAFT)

FP&A reviews any request as goodwill |"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/support-console-record-format-changes-2027.json", "chunk": "3/5", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Support Console: Record Format Changes (April 2027)", "status": "published", "date": "2027-03-29", "text": "## Account field on writes
- On the writable tables (`cases`, `credit_notes`, `disputes`) the account field is now `billing_account_id`, on reads and writes. Its value is the account's `account_id`.
- A write or query on those tables that still sends `account_id` fails with an unknown-field error. Read-only tables keep `account_id`.
## Billing timezone
- Accounts have a `billing_timezone` (an IANA name such as `America/Los_Angeles`; `UTC` unless set).
- Which billing month and invoice line a request belongs to is set by Finance's invoice period rules; see Finance's 2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods (Finance shared drive)."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/finance-and-legal/budgeting-and-forecasting/blended-cost-methodology-v1.json", "chunk": "10/17", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Blended Cost Methodology v1 (Unit Economics Dashboard)", "status": "published", "date": "2025-02-11", "text": "### Versioning rules
- Each rate card release is versioned (e.g., 2025Q4, 2026Q1).
- The Unit Economics Dashboard must:
  - Persist the rate card version used for any aggregate.
  - Allow Finance to rerun historical periods using the version in effect at the time (reporting stability).
### Effective dates
- Monthly rate updates are effective at the start of the month in **UTC**, unless otherwise specified in the release note.
- Finance reporting may use month boundaries in Pacific Time for close processes; where required, Finance will specify a “reporting calendar” mapping. Default dashboard time boundaries remain UTC."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/finance-and-legal/billing-controls/collections-and-dunning-schedule-2027.json", "chunk": "1/1", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Collections: Dunning Schedule for Overdue Invoices (2027)", "status": "published", "date": "2027-01-15", "text": "title: Collections: Dunning Schedule for Overdue Invoices (2027)

body: ## Scope
Invoices still unpaid after their due date, once any automatic payment retries have finished. Payments that fail during a payment-processor incident are retried automatically and are not overdue; this page doesn't apply to them.
## Schedule
| Days past due | Step |
|---|---|
| 3 | Reminder email to the billing contact |
| 10 | Second reminder; account team copied |
| 21 | Final notice |
| 45 | Hosted API access suspended until paid |
## Changes from 2026
From 1 January 2027 the final notice is sent on day 21 instead of day 30.

body: ## Scope
Enterprise accounts that pay by bank transfer against net-30 invoices. They have no card on file, so card autopay and processor retries do not apply to them. This page is not about card payments that fail during a payment-processor incident; see the processor incidents page for those.
## Collections
- Billing Ops sends a reminder 5 days after the due date and retries an ACH pull on day 7.
- Questions go to the account team.

body: > Archived 2026-01-21. This help-center article is no longer current. Support handles duplicate charges as described on "Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes".
## Duplicate charges
If your invoice bills the same usage twice, contact Support with the invoice number. Support refunds a duplicated line in full on request.
## Refund timing
Refunds reach your card within 5-10 business days."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/discounting-and-credits-policy-for-usage-based-products.json", "chunk": "9/20", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Discounting and Credits Policy for Usage-Based Products", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-22", "text": "### Application order (standard)
On each invoice, the billing system applies adjustments in this order:
1. **Included usage** in the customer’s package/free tier (if applicable)
2. **Contracted unit prices** (including any negotiated discount)
3. **Credits** (promotional/contracted/service), applied to the eligible usage subtotal
4. Taxes and non-creditable line items
Important: credits offset charges; they do **not change recorded usage quantities**.
### Cache-hit attribution and billed tokens
If the meter spec distinguishes cached vs uncached billed tokens, credits apply to the final **billed** quantities after cache and dedupe logic. Any customer-visible statement about caching must use approved language from Legal (see related page)."}, {"source": "sources/google_drive/shared_drives/finance/billing-adjustments-approval-matrix.json", "chunk": "2/7", "kind": "Drive doc", "title": "Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix", "status": "final", "date": "2027-02-26", "text": "## Scope

- Marketplace purchases are out of scope: adjustments go through the marketplace (see the marketplace invoicing notes).

## Definitions
- **Adjustment**: any change to what a customer owes after an invoice is issued: a credit note, a refund, a write-off or a re-issued invoice.

- **Billing error**: a line that bills the wrong rate, quantity or product, or bills the same usage twice.
